acceptanceCriteria.statement: deriveUniforms() derives a per-feature footprint-scale factor from radiusEarth and applies it to EVERY footprint-bearing uniform (crater, river/valley, lava-cell/crack, chaos raft, crystal facet, basalt hex, edifice, dune, karst doline, ecumenopolis district, shatter block, sublimation pit/polygon). Footprint frequency rises monotonically with radiusEarth across a 0.4->13 sweep, stays bounded, and the baseline (radiusEarth=1.0) is recalibrated so features occupy a smaller fraction of the disk than the pre-change values. One shared helper, not per-uniform magic numbers.

verifyVia.input: npx vitest run tests/planet-archetypes.test.js (or a new tests/planet-scale.test.js) -- oracle samples the derived footprint uniforms across a radiusEarth sweep 0.4..13
verifyVia.observable: Oracle asserts: monotonic frequency increase with radius for every listed feature, bounded outputs, and baseline-at-r1.0 strictly smaller footprint (higher frequency) than the captured pre-change baseline constants; suite green

acceptanceCriteria.statement: On a radius-1.0 Rocky world at fixed camera distance, craters and rivers occupy a clearly smaller fraction of the disk than the pre-change baseline (features no longer dominate / 'make the planet look small'); AND between two surfaced bodies of different radius (e.g. Titan r0.4 vs Magma r1.5, same camera distance) the larger body shows visibly smaller / more numerous footprints.

verifyVia.input: Lab on :9223, Rocky preset d4 clouds zeroed: screenshot before/after; then Titan vs Magma at matched distance, screenshot pair
verifyVia.observable: Rocky after-shot shows craters/rivers at a visibly smaller disk-fraction than before (measured feature angular size down, pixel-diff >=3%); Titan-vs-Magma pair shows the larger body with the smaller relative footprint

acceptanceCriteria.statement: deriveUniforms() derives an animation-rate factor that decreases monotonically with radiusEarth and applies it to every time-driven uniform (lava emissive-crack pulse / 'breathing' rate, water-glint shimmer rate, gas-giant storm drift, aurora pulse). Baseline rates recalibrated so even a self-sized body no longer 'breathes too fast'. Bounded; one shared helper.

verifyVia.input: vitest oracle: sample the derived rate uniforms across a radiusEarth sweep
verifyVia.observable: Monotonic rate decrease with radius for every listed time-driven uniform, bounded; baseline-at-r1.0 rate strictly below pre-change constants; suite green

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Lava emissive 'breathing' on the Lava/Magma presets is visibly slower than the pre-change rate; gas-giant storm drift on a large giant (Jovian r11.2) is slower than on a smaller giant (Neptune r3.9) at matched playback.

verifyVia.input: Lab on :9223: Lava preset nightside, sample uTime-advanced frames N apart, measure crack-glow phase delta before/after; Jovian vs Neptunian storm-centroid displacement over equal uTime
verifyVia.observable: Lava crack-glow phase advances less per unit time than pre-change; Jovian storm centroid moves less than Neptune's over the same uTime step

acceptanceCriteria.statement: deriveUniforms() scales relief-amplitude uniforms by a bounded function of surfaceGravity (M/R^2) so that low-gravity worlds get amplified relief and high-gravity worlds get subdued relief. Applied consistently to the relief-amplitude knobs; monotonic decreasing in surfaceGravity; bounded to avoid degenerate flat/spiky extremes.

verifyVia.input: vitest oracle: compute derived relief-amplitude factors across all 23 presets and assert ordering by surfaceGravity
verifyVia.observable: Mars/Titan (low g) resolve to higher relief-amplitude factor than Magma/Carbon (high g); factor monotonic-decreasing in surfaceGravity, within [floor, ceil]; suite green

acceptanceCriteria.statement: COARSE (lever 3 is the fuzziest): with terminator-grazing light, Mars and Titan show taller relief shadowing than the pre-change baseline, and a high-gravity world (Magma or Carbon) shows flatter relief than a low-gravity one of similar feature set. Directional sanity check, not a precise magnitude target.

verifyVia.input: Lab on :9223 at a grazing sun angle: Mars and Titan before/after screenshots; Carbon (high g) vs a low-g rocky at matched lighting
verifyVia.observable: Mars/Titan after-shots show longer/deeper relief shadows than before; high-g world reads visibly flatter than the low-g comparator

Edits confined to the deriveUniforms transform; the analytic-gradient / voronoi3d / crater-shape math in core.js is NOT touched. GLSL combiner bodies unchanged except that a uniform value now arrives pre-scaled.
